p.src: Jia She and Jia Zheng now led Jia Zhen and the others away, and nothing more need be said of them. Lady Jia then ordered the folding screens removed and the two tables joined into one. The married maids wiped the table afresh, rearranged the fruit, changed the cups, washed the chopsticks, and set everything out again. Lady Jia and the others put on extra clothing, washed their hands and rinsed their mouths, drank some tea, and only then resumed their seats in a close circle. Lady Jia noticed that Baochai and her sister were absent. Knowing that they had gone home to celebrate the full moon, and that both Li Wan and Xifeng were ill, she felt the gathering much diminished and lonelier for the absence of those four. Lady Jia said with a smile, “In former years, when your husbands were away from home, we would simply invite your aunt over, and everyone would admire the moon together in great merriment. Yet whenever we suddenly thought of your husbands, we could not help reflecting that mothers and sons, husbands and wives, and parents and children could not be together, and our spirits would fall. This year, now that your husbands are here, we ought properly to enjoy a happy family reunion, but it would not be convenient to invite those ladies and their children over to talk and laugh with us. Besides, two more people have joined their household this year, so they could hardly leave them behind and come running over here. And as ill luck would have it, our girl Feng has fallen sick. With her here to talk and laugh, she alone could fill the place of ten people. It only goes to show that nothing in this world can ever be perfect.” When she had finished speaking, she could not help heaving a long sigh, and ordered large cups to be brought and filled with warm wine. Lady Wang smiled. “Being reunited today as mother and sons is naturally more enjoyable than in former years. Though there were more women and children here in past years, that could never compare with the happiness of having all one’s own flesh and blood together this year.” “That is precisely why,” Lady Jia replied with a smile, “I was so pleased that I called for a large cup of wine. You must all change to large cups as well.” Lady Xing and the others had no choice but to change to large cups. It was late, they were tired, and none of them could hold much wine, so they inevitably began to feel weary. But Lady Jia’s enjoyment had not yet waned, and they had no choice but to keep drinking with her. Lady Jia next ordered felt rugs spread upon the steps and had the mooncakes, watermelons, fruit, and other refreshments carried down, so that the maids and married servants might also sit together in a circle and admire the moon. Seeing that the moon had reached the zenith and looked even more brilliant and lovely than before, Lady Jia said, “With such a beautiful moon, we cannot do without the sound of a flute.” She therefore sent for the girls from the ensemble. Lady Jia said, “Too much music would only spoil the refinement. It will be enough to have the flute player perform at a distance.” As soon as she had spoken and the girl was about to go and play, one of Lady Xing’s attendant women came over and whispered a few words to her mistress. Lady Jia at once asked, “What is it?” The woman replied, “Just now, as the Elder Master was leaving, he tripped over a stone and sprained his leg.” On hearing this, Lady Jia hurriedly ordered two elderly women to go and see how he was, and told Lady Xing to go quickly as well. Lady Xing accordingly took her leave and rose to go. Lady Jia then added, “Zhen’s wife, you may as well take this opportunity to go home too. I shall be going to bed shortly.”

p.src: Madam You smiled. “I am not going home today. I am determined to stay and drink with our Old Ancestress all night.” “That will never do, never do,” Lady Jia replied with a smile. You are still a young married couple. Should you not enjoy your own reunion tonight? How could I keep you from it?” Madam You blushed and said with a laugh, “Old Ancestress, you make us sound quite shameless. Though we may still be young, we have been husband and wife for more than ten years and are both nearing forty. Besides, our period of mourning is not yet over. It is proper enough for me to spend the night keeping you company, but how could we possibly go off to enjoy a reunion by ourselves?” Hearing this, Lady Jia smiled. “Quite right. I had forgotten that your mourning period is not yet over. Poor father-in-law of yours has been gone for more than two years, and yet I forgot. I deserve to be fined a large cup. In that case, do not trouble to see her off; stay here and keep me company. Have Rong’s wife escort her out, and she can go home at the same time.” Madam You relayed the instruction. Rong’s wife assented and escorted Lady Xing out. They went together as far as the main gate, then each boarded her own carriage and returned home. Nothing more need be said of them.

p.src: Grandmother Jia remained there with the others for a while, admiring the osmanthus blossoms, before returning to the banquet and having warm wine brought in. As they chatted idly, they suddenly heard, from beneath the osmanthus trees across the way, the plaintive, lingering strains of a flute. With the bright moon and pure breeze, beneath a clear sky and over tranquil ground, the music truly swept away every vexation and dispelled every care; all sat upright in solemn silence, listening in appreciation. After a time sufficient to drink about two cups of tea, the music finally ceased, and everyone praised it without end. More warm wine was then poured. Grandmother Jia smiled. “Was it truly worth hearing?” “It was indeed,” everyone replied with a smile. “We would never have thought of arranging anything like it. Only with Your Ladyship to lead us can we broaden our hearts a little.” “That was not yet the best,” said Grandmother Jia. “The slower the melody they choose, the better it will sound.” As she spoke, she ordered that one of the palace-made mooncakes she herself had been eating, filled with melon seeds, pine nuts, and rich paste, together with a large cup of hot wine, be sent to the flautist, who was to eat and drink at leisure before playing another full suite with greater delicacy. The married servants assented and had just sent these things away when the two old women who had gone to look after Jia She returned. “The top of his right foot is a little pale and swollen,” they reported. “He has now taken the prescribed medicine, and the pain is better. It is nothing very serious.” Grandmother Jia nodded and sighed. “I worry far too much. “For all his insistence that I am partial, look how concerned I am about him!” She then repeated Jia She’s earlier joke to Lady Wang, Madam You, and the others. Lady Wang and the others smiled and consoled her. “It was only a little joking among everyone after drinking; careless remarks are bound to occur. How could he possibly dare accuse Your Ladyship? “You should set your mind at ease.” Just then, Yuanyang arrived with a soft hood and a large cloak. “It is late,” she said. “I fear the dew will fall and the wind chill your head, so you must put these on. “You have sat long enough; it is time to rest.” “I happen to be enjoying myself today, and here you are urging me to leave,” said Grandmother Jia. “Do you suppose I am drunk? I mean to stay until dawn!” She then ordered more wine to be poured. She put on the hood and wrapped herself in the cloak while everyone continued drinking with her and exchanging jokes. Then, from the shadow of the osmanthus trees, there came once more a thread of flute music, sobbing and wavering, drifting softly on the air; it was indeed more desolate than before. Everyone sat in silence. The night was still and the moon bright, while the flute sounded sorrowful and aggrieved. Grandmother Jia, elderly and warmed by wine, could not help being touched to the heart by the music, and tears began to fall. A sense of desolation and loneliness stole over all of them. Only after some time did they notice Grandmother Jia’s grief; then they hurriedly turned toward her with smiles, speaking reassuring words to comfort her. They ordered the wine warmed again and had the flute stop for the time being. Madam You smiled. “Let me try telling a joke as well, to divert Your Ladyship.” Grandmother Jia forced a smile. “That would be even better. Quickly, let me hear it.”

p.src: Madam You began: “A certain family had four sons. The eldest had only one eye, the second only one ear, and the third only one nostril. The fourth had everything he should—but unfortunately he was mute.” She had reached this point when she saw that Grandmother Jia’s eyes had grown hazy and that she seemed to be falling asleep. Madam You stopped, and she and Lady Wang hurriedly roused her with gentle words. Grandmother Jia opened her eyes and smiled. “I am not sleepy; I merely closed my eyes to rest them. “Go on talking. I am listening.” Lady Wang and the others smiled. “It is already the fourth watch, and the wind and dew are heavy. Please retire for the night, Your Ladyship. “Tomorrow you may admire the moon on the sixteenth as well, and so do full justice to its beauty.” “How can it be the fourth watch already?” asked Grandmother Jia. Lady Wang smiled. “It truly is. The young ladies could not endure staying awake and have all gone to bed.” Hearing this, Grandmother Jia looked around carefully. Sure enough, they had all dispersed, and only Tanchun remained. Grandmother Jia smiled. “Very well, then. “You are not accustomed to staying up either; besides, some are frail and some are ill. It gives me less to worry about now that they have gone. “Only poor Third Girl has stayed here waiting all this time. “You go too. We shall break up now.” With that, she rose and took a sip of plain tea. A sedan chair fitted with a bamboo seat had already been prepared; wrapped in her cloak, she sat in it, and two old women lifted it while the others clustered around and followed her out of the garden. There is no need to dwell on this.

p.src: Meanwhile, as the married servants cleared away the cups, plates, bowls, and dishes, they discovered that a fine teacup was missing. After searching everywhere without finding it, they questioned the others. “Someone must have dropped and broken it. “Just tell me where the pieces were left, so that I can take the shards back as proof when accounting for it. Otherwise they will accuse someone of stealing it.” “No one here broke it,” they all replied. “Perhaps one of the maids attending the young ladies did; that is also possible. “Think carefully, or go and ask them.” This reminded the woman responsible for the tableware. “That is right,” she said with a smile. “I remember now that Cuilü was holding it at the time. “I shall go and ask her.” She went off to look for her, and had only just descended onto the paved walk when she met Zijuan and Cuilü approaching. Cuilü asked her, “Now that the Old Lady’s party has ended, do you happen to know where our young lady has gone?” “I came to ask where that teacup went,” replied the woman, “yet here you are asking me for your young lady!” Cuilü laughed. “I was pouring tea for my young lady, but when I turned my head for just a moment, not only the cup but even she was gone.” “Her Ladyship said just now that they had all gone to bed,” said the woman. “You must have gone off somewhere amusing yourself and failed to notice.” Cuilü said to Zijuan, “There is no possibility that she would have slipped away to bed without a word. She must have gone for a walk somewhere. “Perhaps, seeing that the Old Lady’s party had ended, she hurried ahead to see her off. “Let us go and look up ahead first. “Once we find our young lady, your teacup will naturally turn up as well. “You can look for it again first thing tomorrow morning. What is the hurry?” The woman smiled. “If I know where it is, there is no need to hurry. I shall ask you for it tomorrow, then.” With that, she went back and continued checking and collecting the tableware. Zijuan and Cuilü, meanwhile, went toward Grandmother Jia’s quarters. There is no need to dwell on this.

p.src: As it happened, neither Daiyu nor Xiangyun had gone to bed. Daiyu had seen the many members of the Jia household admiring the moon, yet Grandmother Jia still lamented that there were too few people and that it was not as lively as in former years. Then she had spoken of Baochai and her sister going home to enjoy the moon with their mother and brother. Moved by the scene, Daiyu had gone alone to lean over the railing and weep. Baoyu, meanwhile, had lately lost all interest in everything because Qingwen was gravely ill. After Lady Wang repeatedly told him to go to bed, he had done so. Tanchun, vexed by recent household affairs, had no leisure for amusement. As for Yingchun and Xichun, though both were present, Daiyu had never been particularly close to either of them. Thus only Xiangyun remained to comfort her. She said, “You are an intelligent person. Why assume such an appearance and torment yourself? I am in the same position as you, yet I am not as narrow-hearted as this. Besides, you are often ill. Should you not take better care of yourself? What is infuriating is Sister Bao: every day she talked as though we sisters were so dear to one another, and long ago she said that this Mid-Autumn Festival we must all admire the moon together, revive our poetry club, and compose linked verses. Yet today she has abandoned us and gone off to enjoy the moon with her own family. The club has broken up, and no one writes poetry anymore. Instead, it is those fathers and sons, uncles and nephews who have taken over the field. You know how well Emperor Taizu of Song put it: ‘Beside one’s own bed, how can another be allowed to sleep soundly?’ If they will not compose, then the two of us shall make linked verses and put them to shame tomorrow.” Seeing how Xiangyun tried to console her, Daiyu did not wish to dampen her exuberance and said with a smile, “Listen to all the noise here. How could anyone feel inspired to write poetry?” Xiangyun laughed. “Though admiring the moon on this hill is pleasant, it can never be as delightful as viewing it beside the water. You know that the foot of this slope borders the pool, and that the place nestled in the hollow near the water is Concave Crystal Lodge. That shows how thoughtfully this garden was designed. The high place on the hill is called Convex Emerald; the hollow beside the water is called Concave Crystal. The characters ‘convex’ and ‘concave’ have seldom been used through the ages. Using them directly as the names of pavilions and lodges makes them seem all the fresher and avoids every cliché. You see, these two places are one above and one below, one bright and one shadowed, one high and one low, one by the hill and one by the water. They truly seem to have been built expressly for viewing the moon. Those who love to see the moon small above a lofty hill may come here; those who prefer the radiant moon over limpid ripples may go there. It is only that in common speech these two characters are pronounced like ‘hollow’ and ‘arched,’ which has made them seem vulgar and kept them from common use. Lu Fangweng alone used the character ‘concave’ in the line, ‘A shallow hollow in the ancient inkstone gathers abundant ink,’ yet someone still criticized him for vulgarity. Is that not absurd?” Lin Daiyu said, “Fangweng was by no means the only one to use it. The ancients used it in countless places. There are examples in Jiang Yan’s ‘Rhapsody on Green Moss,’ Dongfang Shuo’s Classic of Divine Marvels, and even the story in the Record of Paintings about Zhang Sengyou painting the Yicheng Temple—far too many to enumerate.

p.src: It is only that people nowadays do not know this and mistakenly treat them as vulgar characters. To tell you the truth, I was the one who proposed these two names. That year, when they tested Baoyu, he proposed names for several places. Some were retained, some were altered or discarded, and some places had not yet been named. Later, all of us devised names for those unnamed places as well, noted the literary sources and described the locations of the buildings, then took the whole collection in for Elder Sister to see. She sent it back out and ordered that it be shown to Uncle. To everyone’s surprise, Uncle was delighted and said, ‘Had I known they could do this, I ought to have asked all the sisters to propose names that day. Would that not have been amusing?’ So every name I proposed was adopted without changing a single character. Let us go to Concave Crystal Lodge now and have a look.”

That year, when they tested Baoyu, he proposed names for several places. Some were retained, some were altered or discarded, and some places had not yet been named.
Later, all of us devised names for those unnamed places as well, noted the literary sources and described the locations of the buildings, then took the whole collection in for Elder Sister to see.
She sent it back out and ordered that it be shown to Uncle.
To everyone’s surprise, Uncle was delighted and said, ‘Had I known they could do this, I ought to have asked all the sisters to propose names that day. Would that not have been amusing?’
So every name I proposed was adopted without changing a single character.
Let us go to Concave Crystal Lodge now and have a look.”

p.src: So saying, the two of them descended the slope together. As soon as they rounded a bend, they came to the edge of the pool, where a continuous bamboo railing followed the path all the way to Lotus-Fragrance Pavilion on the far side. These few rooms nestled in the embrace of the hill and served as a secluded retreat belonging to Convex Emerald Villa. Since the ground was hollow and close to the water, the plaque over the entrance read “Concave Crystal Creek Lodge.” Because there were few rooms here and they were small and low, only two old serving-women kept watch at night. That day, learning that the staff of Convex Emerald Villa had been assigned to serve and that the duty had nothing to do with them, the two old women had shut themselves in with mooncakes, fruit, wine, and food given as rewards. After eating and drinking their fill, they had long since put out the lamps and gone to sleep. When Daiyu and Xiangyun saw that the lamps had been extinguished, Xiangyun laughed and said, “It is just as well that they are asleep. Why do we not sit beneath this curved roof and admire the moon beside the water?” The two of them accordingly sat down on a pair of stools made of mottled bamboo. A brilliant full moon shone in the sky, while another moon floated in the pool below. The two vied in radiance, making them feel as though they were within a crystal palace in the chambers of the merfolk. Whenever a light breeze passed, the shimmering surface of the pool wrinkled into patterns of jade-green ripples, truly cleansing both mind and spirit. Xiangyun laughed. “How delightful it would be if we could sit in a boat and drink wine just now. If this were at my home, I would get into a boat at once.” Daiyu laughed. “The ancients were right to say, ‘If everything must be perfect, what joy can there be?’ In my opinion, this is pleasant enough. Yet you insist on wanting a boat as well.” Xiangyun laughed. “After gaining Long, one longs for Shu; that is simply human nature. That shows the old people were quite right in what they said. They say that poor families imagine everything goes exactly as wealthy families wish. If you tell them that the wealthy, too, cannot have everything their way, they refuse to believe it; only after experiencing such circumstances themselves do they come to understand. Take the two of us: though we have no parents with us, we have nonetheless been privileged to live amid wealth and honor, yet you and I still have so many disappointments.” Daiyu laughed. “It is not only you and I who cannot have our wishes fulfilled. Even the Old Lady and Lady Wang, down to Baoyu, that girl Tanchun, and the others—whether the matter is great or small, reasonable or unreasonable—the principle is the same: none can have everything go as they wish. How much more must this be so for you and me, mere guests lodging away from home!” Hearing this, Xiangyun feared that Daiyu would grow melancholy again and hurriedly said, “Enough of this idle talk. Let us compose linked verses.”

p.src: As they were speaking, the melodious strains of a flute rose into the air. Daiyu smiled. “The Old Lady and the ladies are in high spirits today. This flute is delightful—it adds to our own enjoyment too. Since we both favor five-character lines, let us compose a regulated sequence in that form.” “Which rhyme shall we use?” asked Xiangyun. Daiyu smiled. “Let us count the upright bars of this railing, from this end to the other. Whichever number we reach will determine the corresponding rhyme category. If there are sixteen, we shall begin with ‘First Xian.’ Is that not a novel idea?” Xiangyun laughed. “That is original.” The two rose and counted from one end to the other; there were exactly thirteen bars. “Of all things, it has to be ‘Thirteenth Yuan’ again,” said Xiangyun. There are so few rhymes in that category that a regulated sequence may become forced and difficult to rhyme. You had better begin with the first line.” Daiyu laughed. “Then we shall see which of us is stronger. The only trouble is that we have no brush and paper to record it.” “That does not matter,” said Xiangyun. “We can write it down tomorrow. p.src: Before she had finished speaking, a figure emerged from behind the rocks beyond the railing and said with a laugh, “Fine poetry, fine poetry! But it is indeed too mournful. There is no need to continue. If all that follows remains in this vein, these two lines will cease to stand out, and the rest will seem merely labored and contrived.” Caught unawares, the two girls started in fright. Looking closely, they saw that it was none other than Miaoyu. Both were astonished and asked, “How did you come here?” Miaoyu laughed. “I heard that you were all admiring the moon, and the flute was being played so beautifully, so I too came out to enjoy the clear pond and the bright moon. My steps happened to bring me here, and when I heard you two linking verses, I found them so exceptionally pure and elegant that I stopped to listen. Yet among the lines I just heard, several are excellent but altogether too dispirited and sorrowful. Such things arise in connection with a person’s allotted destiny, and that is why I came out to stop you. The Old Lady and the others dispersed long ago, and I expect everyone in the garden is now fast asleep. Your maids must be searching everywhere for you, without knowing where you are. And are you not afraid of the cold? Come with me quickly and have a cup of tea at my place. Before long, I fear, it will be daylight.” Daiyu laughed. “Who would have thought it was already so late?”

p.src: The three of them then went together to Green Lattice Nunnery. The flame before the shrine still burned blue, and the incense in the burner was not yet spent. Several old nurses had fallen asleep, and only a little maid sat nodding on a rush cushion. Miaoyu woke her and told her to make fresh tea. Suddenly there came a knock at the gate. The little maid hurried to open it and found Zijuan and Cuilü, accompanied by several old nurses, searching for the two young ladies. When they came in and saw them drinking tea, they all laughed. “How you have made us search! We went through the whole garden and even looked at your aunt’s quarters. Just as we reached the little pavilion at the foot of the hill to look there, the night watch happened to wake up. We asked them, and they said that two people had been talking beneath the awning outside the pavilion, that another later joined them, and that they heard them say they were all going to the nunnery. Then we knew you must be here.” Miaoyu promptly told the little maid to take them to another room, where they could sit, rest, and have tea. She herself brought out brush, inkstone, paper, and ink, asked the other two to recite the poem they had just composed, and wrote it down from the beginning. Daiyu, seeing Miaoyu in exceptionally high spirits that day, smiled and said, “I have never seen you so cheerful before. I would not presume to ask for your instruction, but might this poem still be worthy of your criticism? If it is worthless, we shall simply burn it; but if it can be put right, please revise it for us.” Miaoyu smiled. “I would not presume to offer reckless praise or criticism. But so far there are only twenty-two rhymes. It seems to me that you have already produced your finest lines, and if you continue, you may lack the strength to sustain them. I should like to add my own poor sequel, though I fear it may mar the poem.” Daiyu had never seen Miaoyu compose poetry, and finding her so enthusiastic now, she hastened to say, “If that is truly what you mean, then even though our part is poor, yours will redeem it.” Miaoyu said, “Now that we are to conclude it, we must ultimately return to our true character. p.src: Afterward she inscribed: “Thirty-five Rhymes of Linked Verse on the Mid-Autumn Night Scene in Prospect Garden.” Daiyu and Xiangyun praised it without cease, saying, “This shows how every day we neglect what is close at hand and seek afar. Here we have such an immortal poet in our midst, yet day after day we merely discuss poetry on paper.” Miaoyu smiled. “We can polish it tomorrow. It must be nearly dawn now; you really ought to get some rest.” At this, Lin Daiyu and Shi Xiangyun rose, took their leave, and went out with their maids. Miaoyu escorted them outside the gate, watched until they were far away, and only then closed the gate and went back in. There is no more to tell of this.

p.src: Meanwhile Cuilü said to Xiangyun, “There are still people at the Young Mistress’s quarters waiting for us to come back to sleep. Where had we better go now?” Xiangyun laughed. “Tell them on your way past that they should go to sleep. If I go back now, I am bound to disturb the invalid. I may as well trouble Miss Lin for half the night instead.” As they spoke, they all made their way to the Naiad’s House, where half the household had already gone to sleep. The two went inside, removed their ornaments, loosened their clothes, washed, and finally went to bed. Zijuan lowered the gauze bed-curtains, moved the lamp away, closed the door, and went out. But Xiangyun was unable to sleep in an unfamiliar bed, and though her head lay on the pillow, she could not fall asleep. Daiyu, deficient in vitality and blood, often suffered from insomnia; today she had also stayed awake past the moment when drowsiness came, so naturally she could not sleep either. The two tossed and turned upon their pillows. Daiyu asked, “Why are you still awake?” Xiangyun smiled faintly. “I cannot sleep in a strange bed, and besides, my drowsiness has passed, so all I can do is lie here. Why can you not sleep either?” Daiyu sighed. “My sleeplessness is hardly limited to tonight. In the course of a whole year, I suppose there are scarcely ten nights when I sleep my fill.” Xiangyun said, “That is because of your illness, and so...” What she said next is not yet known; listen to the explanation in the following chapter.
